o.text: From Arabic قَرَنْفُل (qaranful), maybe through Ottoman Turkish قرنفل or Persian قرنفل.
From Proto-Common Turkic *oŋurtka, derived from Proto-Common Turkic *oŋur, from Proto-Common Turkic *oŋ-.

Onomatopoeic. Equivalent to bar + -qır. Cognate with Old Turkic [script needed] (bakïr-), Turkish bağırmak, Crimean Tatar bağırmaq.
The root shows itself in bar-bar bağırmaq (“shouting loudly”).
From Proto-Turkic *oklagu (“rolling pin”). Cognate with Bashkir уҡлау (oqlaw, “rolling pin”), Kazakh оқтау (oqtaw), Turkish oklava, Uzbek oʻqlogʻi, oʻqlov, etc.
